subject: environmental
audience: FE Environmental candidates and environmental engineering students
title: The Scrubber That Left 4 lb/hr, Not 36
featured_title: THE SCRUBBER THAT LEFT 4 LB PER HOUR, NOT 36

presentation.challenge: The scrubber removed 36 lb/hr, but that was not the stack emission. Only 4 lb/hr remained after 90% control.

practice.primary_question: How are an emission factor, process rate, and control-device efficiency combined to calculate an emitted pollutant rate?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Calculating the pollutant mass removed by the control device and reporting that removed mass as the stack emission rate.

case_dna.target_misconception: A 90% efficient scrubber on a 40 lb/hr uncontrolled source emits 36 lb/hr because 90% of 40 is 36.
case_dna.why_plausible: The multiplication is numerically correct, but it calculates pollutant captured, not pollutant remaining in the exhaust.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: Uncontrolled emissions are 4.0 ton/hr×10 lb/ton=40 lb/hr. A 90% device removes 36 lb/hr, leaving 4 lb/hr emitted.
case_dna.corrected_model: First calculate uncontrolled emissions. Then multiply by the uncontrolled fraction remaining, 1-η, to obtain the controlled emission rate.

problem_statement: A boiler burns 4.0 ton/hr of fuel. The uncontrolled particulate emission factor is 10 lb/ton of fuel. A scrubber removes 90% of the particulate entering it. A note calculates 40×0.90=36 lb/hr and labels that value as the stack emission rate. Determine the uncontrolled emission rate, particulate removed, and actual emitted rate.
fixed_constraints: No other particulate sources or sinks

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The 36 lb/hr calculation measured capture, not release.
gates.prompt: What fraction of particulate remains after a 90% efficient control device?

options.label: Econtrolled=Euncontrolled(1-η)
options.reason: The control efficiency is the fraction removed, so 1-η is the fraction emitted.

options.label: Econtrolled=Euncontrolledη
options.reason: That computes mass captured by the device, not mass leaving the stack.

options.label: Econtrolled=Euncontrolled/η
options.reason: Dividing by efficiency does not represent a removal process.

gates.label: Predict
gates.heading: Predict the stack emission rate
gates.prompt: Enter the controlled particulate emission rate in lb/hr.

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Close the particulate mass balance
gates.result: The controlled stack emission rate is 4 lb/hr.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the emitted rate
gates.success: Uncontrolled=40 lb/hr, removed=36 lb/hr, emitted=4 lb/hr.
gates.hint: Use the 10% that remains after 90% removal.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: Removal efficiency splits the uncontrolled mass rate

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the stack-emission note
report: C3. Therefore the stack emits 36 lb/hr.

claims.label: C2
claims.reason: This is the stated removal efficiency.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: It reports captured mass instead of the mass remaining after control.

evidence_choices.label: 40(1-0.90)=4 lb/hr
evidence_choices.reason: This calculates the uncontrolled fraction that remains in the exhaust.

correction.template: Uncontrolled emissions are {uncontrolled} lb/hr, {removed} lb/hr is captured, and {emitted} lb/hr is emitted.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Meet a 3 lb/hr stack limit
gates.constraint: Keep the uncontrolled emission rate at 40 lb/hr.

options.label: Keep 90% efficiency
options.reason: That leaves 4 lb/hr, above the 3 lb/hr limit.

options.label: Allow 97.5% of the pollutant to remain

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply the same emission calculation
gates.prompt: A process uses 6 ton/hr, has an emission factor of 8 lb/ton, and 85% control. What is emitted?

options.label: 40.8 lb/hr
options.reason: That is the mass removed, not emitted.

options.label: 48 lb/hr
options.reason: That is the uncontrolled emission rate.

gates.explanation: Controlled emissions equal the uncontrolled rate multiplied by the fraction not removed.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the emissions calculation
gates.confirmation: I confirm that control efficiency describes the fraction removed and that the stack emission rate uses the remaining fraction.

items.label: What failed
items.value: Captured particulate was reported as emitted particulate.

items.label: What was missed
items.value: Only the fraction 1-η remains after control.

seo.seo_title: Emission Factor and Control Efficiency | FE Environmental E-074
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Environmental Case E-074: a 40 lb/hr uncontrolled particulate source with 90% removal emits 4 lb/hr, not 36 lb/hr.
seo.focus_keyphrase: FE Environmental emission factor control efficiency
seo.excerpt: Control efficiency tells you what is removed, not what is emitted. Stack emissions use the fraction that remains.
seo.direct_answer: The uncontrolled rate is 4.0 ton/hr×10 lb/ton=40 lb/hr. A 90% scrubber removes 36 lb/hr, leaving 40(1-0.90)=4 lb/hr emitted.

faqs.q: How do you calculate controlled emissions from a removal efficiency?
faqs.a: Multiply uncontrolled emissions by 1 minus the control efficiency.

faqs.q: What removal efficiency is required to reduce 40 lb/hr to 3 lb/hr?
